title: doppeldata manifest
description: The record of a generated dataset, which with its profile and scenario regenerates every file byte for byte.

kind.description: Always `table`: the manifest of one table's files.

tool.description:
The tool that wrote the files, as `doppeldata <version>`. The files' bytes are a function of
the identity and this version.

dataset_digest.description: `sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of `identity`'s RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

scenario.description: The scenario applied, or null for none.

destination.description: Where the files were written, as the caller named it, such as `s3://bucket/orders/`.

files.description:
Every object of the rows written, in path order. Under `cdc` these are the full-load
files, and `cdc` lists the change files and the expected table.

faults.description:
The faults the write's fault list holds, counted by kind, or null for a write that lists
none: one with no `malformed_rows`, and no `cdc` with a fault rate. A partial manifest counts
the faults of the objects it lists.

cdc.description:
The change stream and the expected table a `cdc` write adds beside its full load, which
`files` lists. Null for any other write.

partial.description:
True when the run stopped early, so `files` lists only the objects that completed. Such a
manifest is stored as `_manifest.partial.json`, and regenerates nothing.

threads.description:
The threads that generated and encoded in each process that wrote. The count never changes
a byte.

tasks.description:
The tasks a write split across processes divided its ranges among, such as a Spark job's,
or null for a write in one process.

written_at.description: When the write finished, in RFC 3339.

oneOf.description: One JSON array of objects per file.
One JSON object per line.

TableManifestKind.description: The `kind` of a [`Manifest`], which tells it from a [`BundleManifest`] under the same file name.

ManifestIdentity.description:
The values a dataset's rows are a pure function of, keyed and written as the identity's canonical
JSON, so a reader rebuilds `dataset_digest` from them with no mapping.

dataset_rows.description:
The rows generated, in decimal, before any copies a scenario's `duplicates` adds. `files`
gives the rows each file holds.

profile_digest.description:
`sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of the profile's RFC 8785 canonical JSON, as given, before a
scenario's patch. In a bundle, the bundle's, every table inline.

scale.description: The scale a bundle was generated at, in decimal, or null for a table generated alone.

scenario_digest.description:
`sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of the scenario's RFC 8785 canonical JSON, or null for none.
The JSON is taken with each perturbation's `id` resolved, and with `description` and
`expect` left out. A composition's is its composed document's: the patches merged in order,
the perturbations concatenated, and the names joined with `+`. In a bundle, the map of each
table a scenario names to its composed document.

table.description:
The bundle table the rows are of, or null for a table generated alone and for a bundle's own
manifest.

Decimal.description: A 64-bit unsigned integer in decimal, because a JSON number is exact only to 2^53.

path.description: The profile's path as the caller gave it, or null when it came from memory.

embedded.description:
Whether each file `files` and `cdc.expected` list holds the whole profile's canonical JSON,
under the metadata key `doppeldata.profile`, and the scenario's document under
`doppeldata.scenario` where one applies. A `cdc` change file never holds either. Left out
when false.

name.description: The scenario's name. A composition's joins its members' names with `+`.

path.description:
The scenario's path as the caller gave it, or null when it came from memory or composes
several.

document.description:
The canonical document `identity.scenario_digest` is taken over, so the dataset regenerates
with no scenario file.

composed_of.description: The scenarios composed, in order, present only for a composition.

path.description: The scenario's path as the caller gave it, or null when it came from memory.

digest.description: The scenario's own digest, taken as `identity.scenario_digest` is.

compression_level.description: The codec's level, which must fall in the codec's range. Null takes the codec's default.

row_group_rows.description: The most rows a row group holds.

dictionary_columns.description: The columns written with a dictionary. Null gives every column one.

timestamp_unit.description:
The unit every timestamp column is cast to. Null keeps each column's own. Parquet holds no
seconds unit, so a column at `s` is stored at `ms`, as pyarrow stores it. parquet's Arrow
writer cannot write INT96, so no unit reproduces it.

oneOf.description: LZ4_RAW, the LZ4 codec current readers expect.

ParquetStatistics.description: How much of the min, max and null count each column chunk records.

oneOf.description: Per column chunk.
Per page too, with the page index.
The random-access file format, `.arrow`.
The streaming format, `.arrows`.

DelimitedSettings.description: A CSV or TSV dialect. Every character must be ASCII.

delimiter.description: Null takes the format's own: `,` for CSV, a tab for TSV.

escape.description: The character that escapes a quote inside a quoted field. Null doubles the quote instead.

header.description: Whether the first line names the columns.

null.description:
What a null prints where the column's profile gives no missing token for it. When it is
empty, an empty string is quoted so the two read back apart.

date_format.description: A chrono format for date columns. Null writes ISO 8601.

timestamp_format.description: A chrono format for timestamp columns without a time zone. Null writes ISO 8601.

timestamp_tz_format.description: A chrono format for timestamp columns with a time zone. Null writes ISO 8601 with the offset.

time_format.description: A chrono format for time columns. Null writes ISO 8601.

bom.description: Whether the file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark.

compression_level.description: The codec's level, which must fall in the codec's range. Null takes the codec's default.

Quoting.description: Which fields are quoted. A null is never quoted.

oneOf.description:
Only a field holding the delimiter, the quote or a line break, and an empty string where a
null prints empty.
Every field that does not parse as a number.
None, even where a field needs it.
windows-1252, the superset of ISO-8859-1 every decoder applies to a `latin1` label.

explicit_nulls.description: Whether a null field is written as `null` rather than left out.

compression_level.description: The codec's level, which must fall in the codec's range. Null takes the codec's default.

LayoutSettings.description: How rows are split into files and directories.

partition_by.description:
The columns whose values name each object's directories, outermost first. A partition
column is left out of the files, because its value is in the path.

partition_values.description:
The values the partition keys take together, as the profile counts them. A range holds
`file_rows` times this, so each of its objects lands near `file_rows` rows.

FileRows.description: The rows each object holds, before a range is scaled by its partition values.

anyOf.description: The same count in every range but the last.

Each range's count drawn from these quantiles, from a stream keyed by the seed, so the
split is the same on every run.

Quantiles.description: Values at named quantiles: p05 is the 5th percentile, p50 the median, p999 the 99.9th. The digits after p are the level's decimal digits, at least two and never ending in 0 past the second.

oneOf.description: `key=value` directories.
Bare value directories, one level per key.

ManifestFile.description:
One object the run wrote. A row or byte count is a JSON number, exact to 2^53 rows, which no
dataset reaches.

path.description: The object's path under the destination, `/`-separated.

range.description: The index of the row range the object holds, which its file name also carries.

first_row.description: The dataset row the range starts at.

range_rows.description: The rows the range holds. A partitioned range splits them across one object per value.

sha256.description: `sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of the object's bytes.

partition.description:
Each partition key's value in the object's path, null for a null value. Absent when the
dataset is not partitioned.

FaultKind.description: One way a file is broken. A row kind breaks one record, and a file kind a whole file.

oneOf.description: A record ending before its last 1 to n − 1 fields.
A record carrying 1 or 2 fields past the last.
A lone quote inside a quoted field.
A line break inside a quoted string field, which is legal CSV.
`N/A`, `-`, `?` or a unit suffix in place of a typed value, or text of another type.
A lone continuation byte or the bytes C3 28 inside a field.
A record past DuckDB's default `max_line_size`.
The file's last record cut mid-field, with no line break, as a cut-off upload leaves it.
A file starting with the UTF-8 byte order mark.
A file whose records end in LF, CRLF and CR mixed.
A file written with another delimiter than the rest.
A file whose header renames a column or swaps two, its values swapped with it.
A file encoded windows-1252 among UTF-8 ones.
A JSON array among NDJSON files, or an NDJSON file among JSON arrays.
A record missing its closing brace.
A number or boolean written as a string.
A file whose timestamp columns are stored at another unit than the rest.
A file whose timestamp columns are stored as INT96, as Hive and Impala wrote them.
A file whose decimal columns are stored one digit of scale wider than the rest.

StreamFault.description: A fault `cdc` places in a change stream, listed in `_faults.jsonl` beside it.

oneOf.description: A change written a second time, after its key's last change.
A change written after its key's last change, in a later file than its commit time.

ManifestCdc.description: What a `cdc` write adds beside its full load.

style.description: The layout the stream takes, as the op's `style` names it.

prefix.description: Where the full load and the change files lie under the destination, `<schema>/<table>/`.

expected_prefix.description: Where the expected table lies under the destination, `_expected/<schema>/<table>/`.

changes.description: The changes the stream holds, counted by operation, a fault's second delivery left out.

files.description: Every change file, in path order.

expected.description: Every part of the table a correct merge of the stream produces, in path order.

StreamFile.description: One object a `cdc` write stores beside its full load.

path.description: The object's path under the destination, `/`-separated.

sha256.description: `sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of the object's bytes.
